description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol allows a privileged client such as a dock or desktop
shell to control and observe the compositor's show-desktop mode.
In show-desktop mode the compositor minimizes or hides all toplevel
windows to reveal the desktop surface underneath.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document
are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

A singleton global that provides read/write access to the
compositor's show-desktop mode state.

Only one client may bind this interface at a time. The
compositor should reject subsequent bind attempts from other
clients while a binding is already active.

On binding, the compositor immediately sends a show_desktop_state
event carrying the current mode so that the client starts
synchronized.

The client sends set_show_desktop_state to request a mode transition.
The compositor applies the transition at its discretion and
confirms the new state via a show_desktop_state event. The
compositor may also emit show_desktop_state spontaneously when
the mode changes through other means (e.g. a keyboard
shortcut or gesture).

Destroy the treeland_show_desktop_v1 object and release
the singleton binding. The compositor will accept a new
binding from another client after this request is processed.

This request does not alter the current show-desktop mode;
the compositor retains whatever state was last set.

Request that the compositor transition to the given
show-desktop mode. The compositor may ignore the request
or apply it asynchronously. If the mode changes, the
compositor confirms the new state by emitting a
show_desktop_state event.

Sending the same mode that is already active is a no-op;
the compositor need not emit a show_desktop_state event in
response.

Emitted by the compositor whenever the show-desktop mode
changes, including once immediately after the client binds
this interface to convey the initial state.

The compositor emits this event both in response to a
set_show_desktop_state request and when the mode changes through
any other compositor-side mechanism.
Describes the current display state of the desktop.
